implementation_notes: NestJS's MVC mode is the TypeScript realization: @Controller('orders') with @Get(':id') is the dispatcher, the method is the worker (injected providers do the work) and @Render('orders/show') names the view while the returned object becomes the template context for the engine configured with app.setViewEngine in main.ts. What replaces the classic structure is Nest's router plus decorator metadata and the template adapter, which keeps the handler strongly typed on both sides; the explicit command-object form is still justified when one endpoint must fan out to several commands, and plain Express + res.render is the smaller alternative when Nest's DI is not wanted.
pitfalls: Providers and controllers are singletons by default: per-request state must come from the request (REQUEST-scoped provider) or method parameters, never from a controller field.
The template context is whatever the method returns - returning a class instance with methods, or an entity with lazy relations, renders surprising values instead of failing.
Mixing @Res() into a @Render handler disables Nest's automatic view rendering; keep response handling out of the handler.
